title: Cap. VII: our sum — praeterition from mere liberty; Paul and Judas
pass_a_gloss: This is the sum of our opinion: that foresight of demerits is not the cause of passing by, non-election or reprobation strictly and properly taken; but as it hangs from the mere good pleasure of God that certain certain persons through special providence, which we call Predestination, are infallibly ordained unto grace and glory, so it hangs from the mere liberty of God that certain other persons are not so ordained, but are destitute of this efficacious grace, and are permitted to fall short of glory. If therefore anyone ask of us why God most easily and most justly could leave both Paul and Judas to their native hardness, and addict them to eternal misery, who also most easily could soften both, and lead them to eternal glory — if, I say, it be asked why he did not prepare for Judas efficacious grace by which he would be softened and saved, and did prepare it for Paul; why he did not ordain Judas infallibly unto glory, and did ordain Paul — we do not flee to the foresighted faith or merits of Paul, nor to the foresighted unbelief or demerits of Judas, but we say that God has mercy on whom he will by softening, and on whom he will he has mercy least by permissively hardening: Nor do we assign another cause of this so diverse providence concerning these persons besides the Will of God, which is the first rectitude. And so you have our opinion.
pass_b_english: Our sum: foresight of demerits is not the cause of praeterition, non-election, or reprobation strictly taken. As it hangs on mere good pleasure that certain persons by that special providence we call Predestination are infallibly ordained to grace and glory, so it hangs on mere divine liberty that others are not so ordained, but left without this efficacious grace and permitted to fall short of glory. If anyone asks why God could most easily and justly leave both Paul and Judas to native hardness and eternal misery — and could as easily soften both and lead them to eternal glory — why he prepared efficacious softening grace for Paul and not Judas, ordained Paul infallibly to glory and not Judas: we do not flee to Paul's foresighted faith or merits, nor Judas's foresighted unbelief or demerits. We say God has mercy on whom he will by softening, and on whom he will he has least mercy by permissive hardening. For providence so diverse about these persons we assign no cause but the Will of God, which is the first rectitude. So you have our opinion.
source_text: Sententiae nostrae haec summa est: Praescientiam demeritorum non esse causam praeteritionis, non-electionis sive reprobationis stricte et proprie sumptae; sed sicuti ex mero Dei beneplacito dependet, quod certae quaedam personae per specialem providentiam, quam Praedestinationem appellamus, infallibiliter ordinentur ad gratiam et gloriam, ita ex mera Dei libertate dependet, quod aliae quaedam personae non ita ordinentur, sed a gratia hac efficaci destituantur, et a gloria deficere permittantur. Si quis ergo a nobis quaerat, cur Deus facillime et justissime potuerit tam Paulum quam Judam duritiae suae nativae relinquere, et aeternae miseriae addicere, qui etiam facillime potuit utrumque emollire, et ad aeternam gloriam perducere — si, inquam, quaeratur cur Judae non praeparaverit gratiam efficacem qua emolliretur et servaretur, Paulo praeparaverit; cur Judam non ordinaverit infallibiliter ad gloriam, Paulum ordinaverit — non confugimus ad praevisam fidem aut merita Pauli, neque ad praevisam Judae infidelitatem aut demerita, sed dicimus Deum misereri cujus vult emolliendo, et cujus vult minime misereri permissive indurando: Neque hujus tam diversae providentiae circa hasce personas aliam causam assignamus praeter Voluntatem Dei, quae est prima rectitudo. Atque sic habetis sententiam nostram.
